decisions.reason: Floor-level shower drainage remains core to the firm's move toward accessible, low-profile systems, and with no evidence of a shortfall against aspirations there is no trigger for problemistic search.
The flagship designer drain embodies the firm's design-quality positioning, so management would protect it rather than withdraw it without clear negative feedback.
The sloped shower element complements the floor-level and renovation range, and the slack of an established firm can carry it while its results remain uncertain.

The backflow-protected basement drain meets a clear safety need and was promoted as a dedicated development, so there is no sign it falls below aspiration, although it is less central to the bathroom focus.
The air-admittance valve is peripheral and only lightly promoted, but it is a low-cost complement within the drainage range, and with no evident shortfall the firm has little reason to drop it.
